doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

chapter: Learning, living and the Colorado years
title: Playing six nights a week at Louie's in Vail
summary: Lamb moved to Colorado, led the trio at Louie's for eight and a half years booking touring players, then a nine-year solo piano gig.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Right. So that was a big deal. And then I moved to the Rocky Mountains, to Colorado in the late 80s and right away got a gig at a club in Vail called Louie’s, which was this jazz club that wanted to happen. And then I was picked as the piano player six nights a week, play with a trio and bring acts in that are traveling, you know Nick Brignola, Ernie Watts, do you remember?
He’s on my list to ask you about.

Oh yeah, so all these cats traveling through, plus local guys: Ron Miles who is a beautiful trumpet player. So I booked this thing for eight and a half years, you know, six nights a week I would play. And I’d do the ski season and then I’d do the summer. I mean it was crazy. So that was that period of time, and then right when that ended I got offered to do a solo piano jazz gig at this club in Vail also. And I did that for nine years. So financially things were cool.
